records.text: ‘Thus says the Lord: This is Jerusalem. I have placed her amid the nations, and the lands around her.
And you will speak My ordinances to the lawless one among the nations, and My laws among the lands around her; for they rejected My ordinances and did not walk in My laws.

Therefore thus says the Lord: Because your impulse comes from the nations around you, and you have not walked in My laws or performed My ordinances—nor have you even acted according to the ordinances of the nations around you—
therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am against you, and I will execute judgment in your midst before the nations,
The lawless person speaks within himself of sinning; there is no fear of God before his eyes.
For he acted deceitfully in his sight, as to finding his lawlessness and hating it.
The words of his mouth are lawlessness and deceit; he was unwilling to understand so as to do good.
He devised lawlessness upon his bed; he stood by every way that was not good, and he was not offended by wickedness.
Woe to those joining house to house and bringing field beside field, so that they may take something from their neighbor! Surely you will not dwell alone upon the earth?
For these things were heard in the ears of the Lord Sabaoth: “If many houses come to be, great and beautiful, they will become deserted, and no one will inhabit them.
For where ten pairs of oxen work, it will yield one jar, and the one sowing six artabas will yield three measures.”
Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard beside the threshing floor of Ahab king of Samaria.

Ahab said to Naboth, “Give me your vineyard, so it may be a vegetable garden for me, because it is nearer my house. I will give you another vineyard better than it; or, if it pleases you, I will give you silver in exchange for this vineyard of yours, and it will be a vegetable garden for me.”
Naboth said to Ahab, “May my God forbid that I should give you my fathers’ inheritance!”
Ahab’s spirit became troubled. He lay on his bed, covered his face, and ate no bread.
Jezebel his wife came to him and said, “Why is your spirit troubled, and why are you not eating bread?”

He said to her, “I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite, saying, ‘Give me your vineyard for silver; or, if you wish, I will give you another vineyard in its place.’ But he said, ‘I will not give you my fathers’ inheritance.’”
Jezebel his wife said to him, “Is this how you now act as king over Israel? Rise, eat bread, and be yourself again. I will give you Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard.”
She wrote a letter in Ahab’s name, sealed it with his seal, and sent the letter to the elders and free men who lived with Naboth.
It was written in the documents: “Observe a fast and seat Naboth at the head of the people.
Seat two men, sons of lawbreakers, opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, ‘He has “blessed” God and the king.’ Let them take him out and stone him, and let him die.”
The men of his city—the elders and free men who lived in his city—did as Jezebel had sent to them, as written in the documents she had sent them.
They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at the head of the people,

Two men, sons of lawbreakers, came and sat opposite him. They testified against him, saying, “You have ‘blessed’ God and the king.” They took him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.
They sent to Jezebel, saying, “Naboth has been stoned and is dead.”
When Jezebel heard, she said to Ahab, “Rise, take possession of Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard, which he did not give you for silver. Naboth is no longer alive; he is dead.”
When Ahab heard that Naboth the Jezreelite was dead, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth. After this, Ahab rose and went down to Naboth the Jezreelite’s vineyard to take possession of it.

And now say to Judah’s men and those dwelling in Jerusalem: Behold, I am shaping evils against you and devising a design against you. Let each turn from his evil way now, and make your practices better.
And they said: We will be resolute, because we will follow our turnings away, and each will do what pleases his evil heart.
“For look, in those days and at that time, when I turn back the captivity of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them over My people and My inheritance Israel, who were scattered among the nations; and they divided up My land
and cast lots over My people; they gave the boys to prostitutes and sold the girls for wine, which they drank.
The men rose and went. Joshua commanded the men going to survey the land, saying, “Go and survey the land and return to me. Here at Shiloh I will bring out a lot for you before the Lord.”
They went, surveyed the land, saw it, and wrote it by its cities in seven portions in a scroll, which they brought to Joshua.
Joshua cast a lot for them at Shiloh before the Lord.
Amaziah said to Amos, “Seer, go! Withdraw to Judah’s land; make your living there, and there you will prophesy.
But you must never again prophesy at Bethel, because it is a king’s sanctuary and a house of kingship.”
Amos answered Amaziah, “I was no prophet or prophet’s son, but a goat herder and one who scratches sycamore figs,
and the Lord took me from the sheep, and the Lord said to me, ‘Go, prophesy to My people Israel.’

I remembered the Lord’s mercy, the Lord’s excellent deeds in everything He repays us. The Lord is a good judge for Israel’s house; He brings upon us according to His mercy and the abundance of His righteousness.
He said, “Are they not My people, children who will surely not reject Me?” And He became their salvation

from every affliction. Neither an envoy nor an angel, but the Lord Himself saved them because He loved and spared them. He Himself redeemed them, took them up, and exalted them throughout all the days of the age.
But they disobeyed and provoked His holy spirit. He turned toward hostility against them and Himself fought them.
sleeping upon ivory beds and indulging upon your couches, eating young goats from the flocks and milk-fed calves from the herds,
clapping to the sound of instruments; they reckoned them as lasting, not passing away,
drinking strained wine and anointing yourselves with the finest perfumes, yet suffering nothing over Joseph’s shattering.
Therefore now they will be captives from the foremost of the powerful, and horses’ neighing will be removed from Ephraim.
Do not defile yourselves in any of these things; for in all these things the nations whom I drive out before your face were defiled,
and the land became defiled, and I repaid them for wrongdoing because of it, and the land became indignant with those settled upon it.
And you shall keep all My statutes and all My commands, and do none of these abominations, neither the native nor the resident foreigner who has joined himself among you—
for the people of the land who were before you did all these abominations, and the land became defiled—
so that the land is not indignant with you when you defile it, as it was indignant with the nations before you.
But if you do not obey Me and do not do these ordinances of Mine,
but disobey them, and your soul is indignant at My judgments, so that you do not do all My commandments, so as to dissolve My covenant,
then I will do this to you: I will bring distress upon you, scab and jaundice that waste your eyes and melt away your life. You shall sow your seeds in vain, and your adversaries shall eat them.
And I will set My face against you, and you shall fall before your enemies. Those who hate you shall pursue you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you.
And if up to this point you do not obey Me, I will discipline you seven times more for your sins.
And I will shatter the arrogance of your pride, and make your heaven iron, and your land as bronze;
and your strength shall be in vain. Your land shall not yield its seed, and the tree of your field shall not yield its fruit.
For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will seek out My sheep and visit them.

As a shepherd seeks his flock on a day when there is gloom and cloud among separated sheep, so I will seek out My sheep and drive them away from every place where they scattered on a day of cloud and gloom.

I will bring them out from the nations, gather them from the countries and bring them into their own land. I will feed them upon Israel’s mountains, in the ravines and in every dwelling place of the land.
I will feed them in good pasture, and their folds will be upon Israel’s high mountain. There they will lie down, there rest in good delight, and graze in rich pasture upon Israel’s mountains.
I Myself will feed My sheep and give them rest, and they will know that I am the Lord. Thus says the Lord, the Lord:
I will seek the lost, bring back the wandering, bind up the broken, strengthen the failing and guard the strong. I will feed them with judgment.
“Amen, amen, I tell you: the one who does not enter the sheepfold through the door, but climbs in from elsewhere, is a thief and a robber.
But the one who enters through the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
To him the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep hear his voice. He calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
When he has brought all his own out, he goes before them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
But they will certainly not follow a stranger; rather, they will flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers.”
